additional_info.subject: RE: 0389458 - ID0389458-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] Unable to charge with DC2 CRM:02023000295
additional_info.body:
Dear Konrad,
Thank you for your patience while I reviewed the logs related to the charging issue you reported.
On
2024-11-12 at 09:05:54
, the charger began the process of initiating a charging session on
Connector 1
. However, within
15-20 seconds
, a session stop request was received from the user, preventing the charger from starting the charging process. As a result, the charger briefly changed to a "faulted" state for approximately
3-4 seconds
.
After this, at
09:07:57
, the charger successfully started charging on
DC2
with
transaction ID: 789803462
, and the session continued until
09:51:01
. Later, the charger initiated another successful charging session on
DC1
with
transaction ID: 280834512
, starting at
11:03:45
and concluding at
11:40:43
.
Both outlets are working fine.
Please let us know if you have any further questions, or if we can proceed to close this ticket.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Vikas Khiladkar

additional_info.subject: RE: 0389458 - ID0389458-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] Unable to charge with DC2 CRM:02023000295
additional_info.body:
Hi,
I would like to do a thorough analysis with you on what exactly happened during this time.
Reported to us:
“We encountered a problem with starting charging at point one. At the station was Jakub M, who authorized himself using a mobile app (android) from his business account (free price list). In the station's logs, we noted the status “Preparing” and then “Accepted” several times - a screenshot of the logs below, yet the app was able to immediately throw the error “Time to connect has expired” (certainly not a timeout).”
{
"id": "1bsgis8feftqkb",
"payload": {
"additionalInfo": {
"callId": "67331a473afce8_82110205"
},
"resourceId": 1242992,
"method": "RemoteStartTransaction",
"payload": "[object] (stdClass: {\"status\":\"Accepted\"})",
"uniqConnectionId": "d952b3d5-e112-4dc1-8181-7b01f127e34d",
"direction": "INCOMING message TO SERVER",
"chargerUuid": "ba13a519-9b6d-4379-ab24-ebfbb2c5b06a",
"message": "INCOMING message TO SERVER"
},
"timestamp": "2024-11-12T09:05:11.439660Z"
The customer then restarted the station, but still had problems on CP1. On CP2 he had no such problems.
A while before the trials, I can see the changes through GetConfiguration, you can see them about time:
2024-11-12T09:01:31.333859+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/22804be356a4[700]: OCPP: Received command: GetConfiguration (conf6733196b3fa1e8_91058629) - {"key":["ConnectionTimeOut"]}
Then on my first attempt at CP1, I see:
2024-11-12T09:05:04.000000+00:00 secc-le [daemon:notice] SECC[848]: {"type":"session_start","timestamp":1731402304311,"chargerId":"secc2300-02193","outlet":"1","outletType":"CCS","payload":{"user":""}}
2024-11-12T09:05:11.437337+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/22804be356a4[700]: OCPP: Send result: RemoteStartTransaction (67331a473afce8_82110205) - {"status":"Accepted"}
2024-11-12T09:05:18.259220+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [DCC] DC1: PilotState "B2" --> "A"
2024-11-12T09:05:18.652299+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] ecog-secc-adapter/d005bedef22d[700]: {"type":"stack_started","timestamp":1731402317000,"chargerId":"","outlet":"","outletType":"CCS"}
2024-11-12T09:05:19.567119+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [DCC] DC1: PilotState "A" --> "E"
2024-11-12T09:05:22.808594+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] ecog-secc-adapter/d005bedef22d[700]: Error: No reply in 4.25s
2024-11-12T09:05:22.810350+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] ecog-secc-adapter/d005bedef22d[700]: at Timeout._onTimeout (/app/node_modules/coap/lib/retry_send.js:74:16)
2024-11-12T09:05:23.862674+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/22804be356a4[700]: secc events: {"type":"SeccSessionStop","outletId":1,"state":{"timestamp":1731402322178,"EVCCID":"","EVMAC":"","SLAC":{"link":"no PLC link","error":false,"init":false},"bookedfor":"","controller":"SECC2300LE",…….
2024-11-12T09:05:25.098837+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/22804be356a4[700]: setOutletLedState error 1
2024-11-12T09:05:25.733029+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/22804be356a4[700]: OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (f2b72c98-3348-4a6d-a5b4-d302e134b322) - {"connectorId":1,"errorCode":"InternalError","status":"Faulted"}
Which coincides with the customer's first situation. Why did EcoG initiate a timeout error at that time?
Second attempt -
Is this where the EV-EVSE connection was disconnected in some way?  Is it simply a loss of communication when the plug is in the socket?
Another attempt with an authentication error - I assume an error on the MSP side.
The session then ran on DC2 without any problem.
Do we have a problem on the CP1 side here? Is he running too slow? Is the problem on the MSP side of not providing information?
With best regards,
Szymon Brodowicz
